## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Katthapaññattivāra* (designated as *Katāpattivāra* in SuttaCentral) is a section of the *Parivāra* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It serves an analytical function by defining the number of sub-offences that may be committed when breaking a monastic rule [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

While SuttaCentral lists no curated parallels in other Buddhist traditions [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus detects extensive internal text reuse across the Pali canon (1,493 matching passages with 80 texts) [DharmaNexus]. The strongest correspondences occur with other catechismal and analytical chapters of the *Parivāra*, especially earlier *Katāpattivāra* sections (Pvr 2.2, Pvr 1.10, Pvr 1.2), the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4), *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 2.16), and *Pārājikakaṇḍa* (Pvr 2.9) [DharmaNexus]. Material is also shared with the *Suttavibhaṅga* (including Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pārājika 2 and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 6) as well as sub-commentarial treatises such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* and *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns several short segments with Tibetan Vinaya treatises, particularly Guṇaprabha's *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
